exposure: SARS-CoV-2 infection in the first trimester
outcome: pregnancy loss before 28 weeks of gestation
cohort: Pregnant women registered at the Obstetrics and Gynecology department of Peking University International Hospital whose last menstrual period was between October 1, 2022, and April 1, 2023, were included in the study.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection in the first trimester significantly increased the risk of gestational hypertension, but did not significantly affect other adverse pregnancy outcomes such as premature birth, neonatal malformation, or altered birth weight.
mod_finding: There was no statistically significant difference in the rate of cesarean section between women with and without SARS-CoV-2 infection in the first trimester.
birth_weight: low birth weight infants, macrosomia, small for gestational age infants
gest_age: premature birth, small for gestational age, pregnancy loss before 28 weeks of gestation
